# RTSTM 2026 — Radiative Transfer in Semi-Transparent Media

**International CNRS Thematic School, organised by the French research
network [TAMARYS](/network/networks/tamarys.html)**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Dates** | 3–9 October 2026 |
| **Venue** | Village vacances Azureva, Hendaye (Pyrénées-Atlantiques), France |
| **Organising committee** | Benoît Rousseau (CNRS, LTeN Nantes) · Laurence Maillé and Paule Lapeyre-Dubosc (Université de Bordeaux) · Léa Penazzi (Aix-Marseille Université) |
| **Sponsors** | SFO, SFT; internationally Eurotherm Committee and ICHMT |
| **Audience** | Doctoral students, researchers and engineers from academia and industry; capacity 65 participants |
| **Languages** | English and French |
| **Official site** | [rtstm.sciencesconf.org](https://rtstm.sciencesconf.org/) |

The school offers general and advanced lectures on radiative transfer in
semi-transparent media (gases, plasmas, particles such as soot and droplets,
and dense and porous materials) and on numerical methods for solving the
radiative transfer equation. It is aimed at problems where radiation cannot be
ignored: decarbonising high-temperature industrial processes and making
spacecraft reusable after hypersonic flight, with relevance also for
atmospheric, fire, urban-thermal and medical science.

## Lectures

| Course | Lecturer | Length |
|---|---|---|
| Basics of thermal radiation | F. Enguehard (Université de Poitiers) | 6 h |
| Methods for solving the RTE | P. Coelho (Instituto Superior Técnico) | 3 h |
| Physics of gas radiation | A. Soufiani (CNRS) | 3 h |
| Approximate gas radiation models | F. Liu (NRC Canada) | 3 h |
| Radiation scattering in particulate media | R. Carminati (ESPCI Paris – PSL) | 1.5 h |
| Radiation physics of solids | B. Rousseau (CNRS) | 1.5 h |
| Near-field radiative transfer | M. Francoeur (University of Utah) | 1.5 h |
| Identification of the radiative properties of semi-transparent media | K. Daun (University of Waterloo) | 1.5 h |
| A history of radiative transfer | P. Mengüç (Özyeğin University) | 2 h |

## Practical sessions

Three sessions of three hours each:

- **Advanced Monte Carlo methods**: R. Fournier (Université de Toulouse) and M. El Hafi (IMT Mines Albi)
- **Infrared thermography and spectroscopy**: G. Parent (Université de Lorraine)
- **Modelling the radiative properties of gases**: F. André (CNRS)

Three evening seminars cover atmospheric re-entry (ArianeGroup), modelling of
high-temperature industrial furnaces (Saint-Gobain) and atmospheric thermal
modelling.

## Why it is listed here

Emissivity is where radiative transfer meets the material. The school's
lectures on the radiation physics of solids and on identifying radiative
properties cover exactly what the laboratories on the
[research map](/network/index.html) measure. Hendaye is also about 1.5 hours
from Bilbao, on the other side of the Bidasoa.
